statement: Every acceptance criterion in the task's triage_note is met on the run's own branch: by tested code that follows specs which agree with each other, or by those specs alone in a docs-only run.

deliverables.where: the task's triage note, in the run's branch
the discovery hand-off, in the run's branch
the plan, in the run's branch
the code report, in the run's branch

judge.stance: The task's acceptance criteria and the files on the run's branch are the truth; everything a step said is a claim to verify. Judge meaning, not wording. Behind every MET, quote the line you relied on, with its path and line number. Grade a criterion PARTIAL, not MET, when its only evidence is lines a search printed. When you searched and then read the file around the line, quote the line from the file you read. A criterion the gate's check verified is graded from the check's finding: quote that finding from the evidence as the line behind its MET, and never grade it UNVERIFIABLE because you cannot run the check yourself.

final.text: Every file the run changed is committed on the run's own branch
final.check_method: Read the git facts of the worktree: no uncommitted change, no untracked file outside the ignore rules

final.text: Every spec the run edited passes the spec rule's structure check
final.check_method: For each edited `*.spec.md`: a Purpose section, at least one behaviour in the fixed pattern with a scenario, at least one acceptance criterion, each behaviour named by a criterion, each criterion naming a behaviour

final.text: No spec the run edited is over 400 lines
final.check_method: Count the lines of each edited `*.spec.md`

final.text: Every id that a spec the run edited links to resolves to exactly one definition
final.check_method: Collect the ids each edited spec links; search the docs folders for each id's definition; fail on none or on more than one

final.text: An acceptance criterion that a split left in a spec may name a behaviour the split moved to another spec, where it keeps its id: the spec rule's structure check reads the id as defined in the spec it moved to, in the run that made the split and in any later run
final.check_method: Index the ids every spec of the repository defines; a criterion may name an id that exactly one other spec defines when the id's prefix is one its own spec defines; no use of the run's base commit

final.text: An acceptance criterion of a spec split from another may name an id of the spec it was split from: the spec rule's structure check reads the id as defined there, in the run that made the split and in any later run
final.check_method: As ts-spec-moved: the split-off spec defines ids with the prefix of the spec it was split from next to its own, and its criteria may name the ids of either

final.text: No spec the run edited has changed on the base branch since the run started
final.check_method: Compare each edited spec at the run's base commit with the same spec at the head of the base branch (`git.base_head`); fail, naming the spec, when the head holds commits the base commit lacks and the spec reads differently at the two; N/A for a run with no base branch and for a run that edited no spec

final.text: Every acceptance criterion the run added or reworded in a spec, and every criterion that proves a behaviour the run added or changed, is named by at least one test that is not skipped
final.check_method: Compare each edited spec with its version at the run's base: the criteria added or reworded, and those proving a behaviour block that changed; search the test folders for each id and read the lines above it for a skip mark; every criterion when there is no base; N/A when the run delivers documents only

final.text: Every verification command the plan lists exits 0 on the branch head
final.check_method: Run each command through the engine's command runner, reusing the code gate's run on an unchanged tree; N/A when the run delivers documents only

final.text: No spec file is edited without a change to a behaviour or an acceptance criterion
final.check_method: Diff each edited spec against the run's base commit; report each file whose diff touches no behaviour block and no criterion row

final.text: No behaviour in a spec the run edited contradicts a behaviour in a spec it links to
final.check_method: Read each edited spec, then each spec it links by id; compare the behaviours that share a subject

scale.met: every pair of behaviours that share a subject states compatible results
scale.partial: one pair differs only in wording that a reader could take two ways
scale.unmet: two behaviours state results that cannot both hold
scale.evidence: the ids of the behaviours compared, with a quote of each

final.text: Each acceptance criterion of the task is achieved by the run's commits
final.check_method: Take the numbered acceptance criteria from the triage note; for each, find the commit content that achieves it

scale.met: each criterion is achieved, by code with a passing test or by a document when the run delivers documents only
scale.partial: each criterion is addressed but one is achieved only in part
scale.unmet: one criterion has nothing in the commits that achieves it
scale.evidence: per criterion number: the path and line that achieve it

read_component.statement: The findings of the reading of one component folder say what the folder holds, or state what was searched, and name the files they rest on

criteria.text: The findings (`component_finding`) of a component folder's reading say what the folder holds and what someone outside depends on, or state what was searched
criteria.check_method: Open each file the findings name at its line ranges or ids, and compare it with what the findings claim

scale.met: the findings say what the folder holds and what someone outside depends on, each claim is in the file it names, or they state what was searched in the folder when nothing was found
scale.partial: the findings cover part of the folder, or a claim is in its file with a different meaning
scale.unmet: the findings describe another folder, claim what the named file does not hold, or say nothing about the folder
scale.evidence: the path and line of each claim checked, and the quote that confirms or refutes it

criteria.text: The findings (`component_finding`) name each file they rest on with its line ranges or ids
criteria.check_method: Read the findings line for the files it names and their line ranges or ids

scale.met: every claim of the findings names its file with the line ranges or ids it rests on, or the findings say what was searched
scale.partial: some claims name a file and others name none
scale.unmet: the findings name no file and say nothing about what was searched
scale.evidence: the claim, and the file and range or id it names

setup.statement: A repository with no overview spec gets one, and one spec per component, that describe the code as it is

criteria.text: The overview spec and every spec the setup note lists pass the spec rule's structure check
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-form plus the line cap, on the overview and on each spec path in the note's component table

criteria.text: Every spec the setup note lists exists and is named by its path in the overview spec
criteria.check_method: Read the note's component table; open each path; search the overview for each path

criteria.text: Every id that a spec of the setup step mentions resolves to exactly one definition
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-links, on the overview and the specs the note lists

criteria.text: No line of a spec the setup step wrote outside a workflow package names that package or its workflow
criteria.check_method: As ts-dis-named, on the overview and each spec of the setup note's component table

criteria.text: Every line of a spec the setup step wrote in words that tie it to a task or a change is reported to the judge as a lead
criteria.check_method: As ts-dis-literal, on the overview and each spec of the setup note's component table

criteria.text: Every line of a spec the setup step wrote with a behaviour sentence over 500 characters, a word two readers could measure differently or a placeholder is reported to the judge as a lead
criteria.check_method: As ts-dis-wording, on the overview and each spec of the setup note's component table

criteria.text: Every behaviour of a spec the setup step wrote has an Evidence row in the setup note with the basis `tested` or `read`, code that exists named with lines inside the file, and an existing test file when the basis is `tested`
criteria.check_method: Read the setup note's `Evidence` table; for each behaviour id of the overview and of each listed spec find its row; check the basis, open each `<path>:<from>-<to>` and compare its line count, open each test path of a `tested` row

criteria.text: Each rule file the setup prompt names (spec.rule.md, extraction.rule.md, task-notes.rule.md, documents.rule.md) that the repository holds under .claude/rules/temperspec/ is opened with the read tool in the session
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: a read call without an error whose target ends in the rule file's name; a search or a failed read does not count

criteria.text: Every file the setup step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every behaviour the setup step wrote describes what the code does now
criteria.check_method: For each behaviour, open the code the setup note names for its component and find where the stated result is produced

scale.met: each behaviour's result is produced by the code as written
scale.partial: each behaviour holds but one cannot be traced because the note names the wrong code for it
scale.unmet: a behaviour states a result the code does not produce
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the path and line that produce the result

criteria.text: Every top-level part of the code base belongs to a component with a spec or is listed as not covered
criteria.check_method: List the top-level folders and entry points; match each with the note's component table and its Not covered list

scale.met: each top-level part is in the component table or under Not covered with a reason
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a top-level part is in neither list
scale.evidence: per top-level part: the component or the Not covered line

triage.statement: The triage note states the task's acceptance criteria, the gaps in the specs, and a route that follows the gaps and the size of the task

criteria.text: The triage note has each section the triage rule requires
criteria.check_method: Read the note's headings against the rule's list

criteria.text: The route follows the gap list: discovery with a gap, plan or quick with none, and quick only within the quick lane's limits and never on a return to triage
criteria.check_method: Compare the route with the gap list and the delivery; for quick, measure the note's criteria count and its Change section against the limits, resolve its commands, and read the visit number

criteria.text: Each rule file the triage prompt names (task-notes.rule.md, documents.rule.md) that the repository holds under .claude/rules/temperspec/ is opened with the read tool in the session
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: a read call without an error whose target ends in the rule file's name; a search or a failed read does not count

criteria.text: Every file the triage step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every acceptance criterion in the triage note is stated by the task
criteria.check_method: Read the task, then each numbered criterion of the note

scale.met: each criterion is a statement the task makes, with none added and none missing
scale.partial: each criterion comes from the task but one is reworded so that its meaning shifts
scale.unmet: a criterion is in the note that the task does not state, or one the task states is missing
scale.evidence: per criterion: the quote from the task

criteria.text: Every concept the task needs that no ready spec covers is listed as a gap
criteria.check_method: Search the spec folders for each concept the task names; compare with the gap list

scale.met: each concept without a ready spec is a gap row, each gap row names the search that found nothing
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a concept has no ready spec yet no gap row lists it
scale.evidence: per concept: the spec path that covers it, or the search that found none

criteria.text: Every gap row that says `Covered by` names a behaviour id and the id of a criterion that names that behaviour, both of one spec and each defined exactly once
criteria.check_method: Read each `Covered by` mark, then look the two ids up in the specs and read the criterion's brackets

criteria.text: With the conversation setting `never`, `blocking` or `always`, the triage note says for every gap row whether the gap is findable or an owner decision, and its `Owner decisions` section gives each owner decision a question, two to four options, a default that is one of them and what a wrong default costs, or says `None`
criteria.check_method: When the conversation value is `never`, `blocking` or `always`, read the sort at the end of each gap row and each entry of the `Owner decisions` section: its question, its options, its default and its cost

discovery_short.statement: A task whose every gap a spec already answers gets a hand-off and a reading list from a short, read-only visit, and a gap the citation does not answer goes on to the full discovery

criteria.text: The short visit's hand-off has each section the task-notes rule requires
criteria.check_method: Read the hand-off's headings in order

criteria.text: The hand-off's `Gaps closed` names every behaviour id a gap row of the triage note cites
criteria.check_method: Read the cited ids of the triage note's gap rows and look for each in `Gaps closed`

criteria.text: The short visit's hand-off lists no changed document
criteria.check_method: Read the hand-off's `Changed documents`: `None`, or nothing but the hand-off itself

criteria.text: The `settled` value is `no` exactly when a line of `Gaps closed` says `Not covered`
criteria.check_method: Compare the value with the `Not covered` lines of the hand-off

criteria.text: The hand-off of a settled short visit has a reading list of at most 10 items, each naming an existing file, the line ranges or ids that matter and one line on why
criteria.check_method: Read the hand-off's reading list: count the items, and each names a file that exists, with its ranges or ids and a reason

criteria.text: The short visit's prompt tells the session to read at most 10 files
criteria.check_method: Read the short visit's prompt file of the package for the reading limit, phrase by phrase

criteria.text: Each rule file the short discovery prompt names (task-notes.rule.md, documents.rule.md) that the repository holds under .claude/rules/temperspec/ is opened with the read tool in the session
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: a read call without an error whose target ends in the rule file's name; a search or a failed read does not count

criteria.text: Every file the short discovery step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts of the worktree after the step's commit

criteria.text: Every behaviour a gap row cites answers that gap's question as the task's acceptance criteria need it, or the hand-off says `Not covered` for the gap
criteria.check_method: Read each gap row, the behaviour and criterion it cites, and the hand-off's line for the gap

scale.met: each gap's cited behaviour states the event, the result and every limit the task's criteria name, or its line says `Not covered` with what is left out
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a gap is taken as answered by a behaviour that leaves out an event, a result or a limit the task needs, or a `Not covered` line names a gap the behaviour does answer
scale.evidence: per gap: the spec path, the behaviour id and the quote that answers the gap, or what it leaves out

read_gap.statement: The findings of the reading of one gap answer the gap, or state what was searched, and name the files they rest on

criteria.text: The findings of a gap's reading answer the gap, or state what was searched
criteria.check_method: Read the gap row in the triage note, then open each file the findings name at its line ranges or ids

scale.met: the findings say what the named files hold about the gap and each claim is in its file, or they state what was searched for the gap's subject when nothing was found
scale.partial: the findings answer part of the gap, or a claim is in its file with a different meaning
scale.unmet: the findings answer another gap, claim what the named file does not hold, or say nothing about the gap
scale.evidence: the gap row, the path and line of each claim checked, and the quote that confirms or refutes it

criteria.text: The findings name each file they rest on with its line ranges or ids
criteria.check_method: Read the findings line for the files it names and their line ranges or ids

scale.met: every claim of the findings names its file with the line ranges or ids it rests on, or the findings say what was searched
scale.partial: some claims name a file and others name none
scale.unmet: the findings name no file and say nothing about what was searched
scale.evidence: the claim, and the file and range or id it names

discovery.statement: Every gap is closed by a spec, a decision record or a research note in the agreed format, committed

criteria.text: Every spec the discovery step wrote passes the spec rule's structure check
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-form, on the files this step changed; the size of a spec is not read here (ts-dis-budget)

criteria.text: Every spec the discovery step wrote is within the repository's spec budget: at most 400 lines and at most 30 KB (30,720 bytes)
criteria.check_method: Count the lines of each spec this step changed or the hand-off lists, the earlier layout included, and the bytes of its file; over means strictly more

criteria.text: A spec over the budget in lines or in bytes fails the discovery check with a finding, carried to the next discovery attempt, that names the spec with its figure over the budget and says to split the spec by capability
criteria.check_method: One fail finding per spec over, with its path, each figure over and the fix `split the spec by capability`; the engine's retry prompt carries each finding to the next attempt

criteria.text: Every document the discovery step created carries its type suffix in its file name
criteria.check_method: Match each new file under the docs folders against the naming table

criteria.text: Every id that a document of the discovery step links to resolves to exactly one definition
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-links, on the files this step changed

criteria.text: Each rule file the discovery prompt names (spec.rule.md, extraction.rule.md, decision.rule.md, research.rule.md, task-notes.rule.md, documents.rule.md) that the repository holds under .claude/rules/temperspec/ is opened with the read tool in the session
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: a read call without an error whose target ends in the rule file's name; a search or a failed read does not count

criteria.text: Every file the discovery step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every gap in the triage note is closed by a document the hand-off names
criteria.check_method: Read the gap rows, then the document the hand-off names for each

scale.met: each gap row has a document whose content settles the gap
scale.partial: each gap has a document but one leaves an open question that blocks planning
scale.unmet: a gap row has no document, or its document does not address the gap
scale.evidence: per gap: the path and the behaviour id or section that settles it

criteria.text: Every behaviour the discovery step wrote states an observable result with no internal name
criteria.check_method: Read each new or changed behaviour; a name is allowed only when someone outside the capability depends on it

scale.met: each behaviour names an event and a result an outside observer could see, with no class, function or module name
scale.partial: each behaviour is observable but one carries an internal name that could be removed without loss
scale.unmet: a behaviour describes how the code works, not what an observer sees
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the quoted sentence

criteria.text: No line the discovery step added to a spec outside a workflow package names that package or its workflow
criteria.check_method: Find the repository's workflow packages (a folder with a `tempergraph.json`, at the top or one folder down) and their folder and workflow names; read the lines the step added to each edited spec outside that package (every line with no base) for those names

criteria.text: Every line the discovery step added to a spec in words that tie it to the task is reported to the judge as a lead
criteria.check_method: Read the lines the step added to each edited spec for words that narrate a change (`no longer`, `any more`, `known limit`, `this change`, `used to`, `as before`, `is now`), an issue reference `#<n>` and the task id; report each as a lead, never a failure

criteria.text: Every line the discovery step added to a spec with a behaviour sentence over 500 characters, a word two readers could measure differently or a placeholder is reported to the judge as a lead
criteria.check_method: Read the lines the step added to each edited spec: a `WHEN … SHALL` line over 500 characters, a vague word (`fast`, `robust`, `secure`, `intuitive`, `appropriate`, `reasonable`, `correctly`, `properly`, `as expected`) in a behaviour line or scenario, a placeholder (`TODO`, `TBD`, `???`, `<…>`) on any line; report each as a lead, never a failure

criteria.text: Every spec the discovery step created is named for its capability: no task id, issue number or leading work verb in its file name, no task id or issue number in its title
criteria.check_method: Find the specs the step created against the run's base (every edited spec with no base); read each file name, without a number prefix, for the task id, `issue-<n>`, `#<n>` and a leading `add`, `fix`, `support`, `remove`, `update`, `implement` or `change`, and its title for the task id and an issue number

criteria.text: Every behaviour the discovery step wrote or changed states a general rule of its capability that reads true to someone who never saw the task and can be read only one way
criteria.check_method: Read each new or changed behaviour and its scenarios against the spec rule's `General rules, not cases` and its wording rules, and against the triage note to see what of the task's own case was copied in

scale.met: each behaviour states the rule of its capability without the task's history, a workflow's name or shape, a test fixture or a reason, reads one way only, and no rule is written twice across specs
scale.partial: each behaviour states a rule, but a scenario carries a value copied from the task or a fixture that could be replaced by an illustrative one without loss
scale.unmet: a behaviour narrates the change or the old defect, names or describes a workflow in a spec outside its package, carries a reason, repeats a rule that another spec owns, or can be read two ways
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the quoted sentence, and for a defect the words that tie it to the task

criteria.text: No document the discovery step wrote covers a concept outside the task's gaps
criteria.check_method: Compare each changed document with the gap rows

scale.met: each changed document maps to a gap row
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a document adds behaviour no gap row asks for
scale.evidence: per document: the gap row it serves

criteria.text: The hand-off of a task that goes on to a plan has a reading list with one item for each file the plan will need, naming an existing file, the line ranges or ids that matter and one line on why
criteria.check_method: Read the hand-off's reading list: each item names a file that exists, with its ranges or ids and a reason

criteria.text: Every discovery prompt tells the session to search for ids and names, to read the line ranges it needs instead of whole files, and to stop reading once each gap has its answer
criteria.check_method: Read each discovery prompt file of the package for the three instructions, phrase by phrase

plan.statement: The plan traces every acceptance criterion to requirements and phases, states its complexity, and agrees with the specs

criteria.text: The plan has each section the plan rule requires, with the status `planned` and a completed mark only on a row that kept its mark through a trip back (KMK-B1 to KMK-B4)
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's headings, its hand-off section, its front matter status and the Completed cell of each row against the rule; for each marked row read the run's history (git log and git show from the base commit) for a marking commit of the run in which the row reads the same, and for a later commit that changed the row's file

criteria.text: Every acceptance criterion in the triage note is named by at least one plan requirement, and in a simple plan by a proof row with its test file and command
criteria.check_method: Match criterion numbers between the note, the plan's requirement table and, for a simple plan, the proof table; a proof row's test is the file of a test row and its command is a listed command

criteria.text: In a simple plan every task row names a requirement of the plan, every requirement is named by a row, and every document under Docs to update is the file of a docs row
criteria.check_method: Match the Req cell of each row against the requirement table, and the paths under Docs to update against the files of the docs rows; N/A for a complex plan, whose rows the expand step writes

criteria.text: The complexity value matches the plan's measured signs
criteria.check_method: Count phases, task rows, test rows, files, commands and reading-set bytes, and read each phase's weight; compare with the rule's limits for `simple`

criteria.text: No requirement or task row says it does less than asked (a stub, a placeholder, for now, a later task)
criteria.check_method: Search the requirement statements and the rows' Change cells for words that cut scope; a hit is a maybe for the judge, never a fail

criteria.text: Each rule file the plan prompt names (plan.rule.md, documents.rule.md) that the repository holds under .claude/rules/temperspec/ is opened with the read tool in the session
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: a read call without an error whose target ends in the rule file's name; a search or a failed read does not count

criteria.text: Every file the plan step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: No plan requirement contradicts a behaviour of a spec the plan references
criteria.check_method: Read each requirement, then the behaviours of each spec the plan references

scale.met: each requirement follows from a behaviour or an acceptance criterion
scale.partial: each requirement is compatible but one goes beyond what any behaviour states
scale.unmet: a requirement states a result a referenced behaviour forbids
scale.evidence: per requirement id: the behaviour id it follows from

criteria.text: The plan prompt tells the session to start from the hand-off's reading list and to open another file only for what the list does not answer
criteria.check_method: Read the plan prompt file of the package for the two instructions, phrase by phrase

expand.statement: Every phase of a complex plan has task rows with tests first and verification commands that run

criteria.text: Every phase of the plan has at least one task row, a completed mark only on a row that kept its mark through a trip back (KMK-B1 to KMK-B4), and the plan's status is still `planned`
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's phase headings, task tables, Completed cells and front matter status; for each marked row read the run's history (git log and git show from the base commit) for a marking commit of the run in which the row reads the same, and for a later commit that changed the row's file

criteria.text: Every code row is preceded by a test row that names an acceptance criterion id, and every acceptance criterion of the task has a proof row with its test file and command
criteria.check_method: Read the row order of each task table, and match the triage note's criterion numbers against the proof table

criteria.text: Every task row names a requirement of the plan, every requirement is named by a row, and every document under Docs to update is the file of a docs row
criteria.check_method: Match the Req cell of each row against the requirement table, and the paths under Docs to update against the files of the docs rows

criteria.text: Every verification command in the plan resolves against the repository's allowed commands
criteria.check_method: Resolve each command with the engine's command resolver, without running it

criteria.text: No task row says it does less than asked (a stub, a placeholder, for now, a later task)
criteria.check_method: Search the requirement statements and the rows' Change cells for words that cut scope; a hit is a maybe for the judge, never a fail

criteria.text: Each rule file the expand prompt names (plan.rule.md) that the repository holds under .claude/rules/temperspec/ is opened with the read tool in the session
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: a read call without an error whose target ends in the rule file's name; a search or a failed read does not count

criteria.text: A task row that names a file that exists in the repository has that file opened by the session with the read tool
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: each existing file a task row names has a read call without an error on its path; a file that does not exist is not asked for

criteria.text: Every file the expand step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every task row implements a requirement of the plan with no change to the plan's design
criteria.check_method: Read the design sections as approved at the plan gate, then each task row

scale.met: each row names the requirement it implements, with the design sections unchanged
scale.partial: each row implements a requirement but one row's file or scope is too loose to act on
scale.unmet: a row implements nothing in the design, or the design sections were rewritten
scale.evidence: per row id: the requirement id

phase.statement: Every row of one phase of the plan is built test first and committed, with each criterion its test rows prove carried by a test

criteria.text: Every row of the phase is marked completed with its date
criteria.check_method: Read the Completed cell of each row of the phase in the plan; the rows of other phases are not read

criteria.text: The file of every row of the phase marked completed changed in the run, whichever attempt or visit changed it (KMK-B8)
criteria.check_method: Compare each marked row's file with the paths the run changed since its base commit; N/A without a base commit

criteria.text: Each criterion a test row of the phase proves is carried by a test in the row's file, and that test is not skipped
criteria.check_method: Open the file of every test row of the phase, find the criterion id of its Proves cell, and read the lines above it for a skip mark

criteria.text: A source file of the phase is not changed before the phase's test files are first written (SRC-B6)
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: no edit or write call without an error on a code row's file of the phase comes before the first write of a test row's file of the phase; N/A where there is no record

criteria.text: Every file the phase changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Each row of the phase has its change in the file the row names
criteria.check_method: Read each row of the phase in the plan, then the line of its file that holds the row's change

scale.met: each row's change is in its file, quoted by path and line
scale.partial: a row's file holds only part of the row's change
scale.unmet: a row marked completed has no part of its change in its file
scale.evidence: per row id: the quoted line of its file

criteria.text: No file is changed that no row of the phase names, apart from the plan's marks and status
criteria.check_method: Read the changed paths the check lists, and match each against the files of the phase's rows

scale.met: every changed file of the phase is the file of a row of the phase, or the plan itself
scale.partial: a changed file is outside the phase's rows but is a natural by-product of a row
scale.unmet: a file that no row of the phase names was changed
scale.evidence: per changed file: the row that names it

code.statement: The whole plan, or the small change of the quick lane, is built test first, committed, with its verification passing in the gate's own run and each criterion carried by a test

criteria.text: Every task row of the plan is marked completed with its date in a plan whose status is `completed`, checked before any command runs
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's Completed cells and status first, and end the check there when one is missing. In the quick lane, read the code report's row table instead

criteria.text: The file of every task row marked completed changed in the run, whichever visit of the code step changed it (KMK-B8)
criteria.check_method: Compare each marked row's file with the paths the run changed since its base commit; N/A without a base commit or in the quick lane

criteria.text: Every verification command the plan lists exits 0 when the gate runs it, whatever the step reported about its own run
criteria.check_method: Run each command through the engine's command runner with the test budget, whatever the step reported in tests_passed

criteria.text: Each criterion a test row proves is carried by a test in the row's file, and that test is not skipped
criteria.check_method: Open the file of every test row (in the quick lane, the note's test files), find the criterion id of its Proves cell, and read the lines above it for a skip mark

criteria.text: A change in the quick lane edits no spec or decision record, only the files its triage note names, at most 2 code files and at most 200 lines
criteria.check_method: Read the changed paths from the git facts and the size of the diff against the run's base; N/A outside the quick lane

criteria.text: Each rule file the code prompt names (task-notes.rule.md, plan.rule.md) that the repository holds under .claude/rules/temperspec/ is opened with the read tool in the session
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: a read call without an error whose target ends in the rule file's name; a search or a failed read does not count

criteria.text: A phase's source files are not changed before the phase's test files are first written
criteria.check_method: Read the session record the engine gives the check: no edit or write call without an error on a code row's file of a phase comes before the first write of a test row's file of that phase

criteria.text: Every file the code step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: The code change agrees by meaning with every behaviour of each spec the run edited
criteria.check_method: Read the changed paths and the edited specs the check lists. For each behaviour of each edited spec, read its scenarios, then the code that implements it. Judge the meaning, not the wording or the names

scale.met: each behaviour's scenarios hold in the code as written, with nothing in the diff that a behaviour forbids
scale.partial: each behaviour holds in its main scenario but one further scenario is not handled by the code
scale.unmet: the code does something a behaviour forbids, or a behaviour of an edited spec has no code
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the file and line of the code that implements it

criteria.text: The code change breaks no behaviour of a related spec that the run did not edit
criteria.check_method: Related specs are those an edited spec links by id plus those the plan references; the check lists them. Read their behaviours against the changed code

scale.met: no behaviour of a related spec is contradicted by the diff
scale.partial: no contradiction, but one related behaviour now depends on code the diff changed with no test that covers it
scale.unmet: the diff makes a behaviour of a related spec false
scale.evidence: per related spec: the behaviour ids read, with the diff lines compared

criteria.text: Each task row's change is in the file the row names
criteria.check_method: Read each row, then the file it names

scale.met: each row's change is present in its named file
scale.partial: each row's change exists but one sits in a different file than the row names
scale.unmet: a row is marked done with no matching change
scale.evidence: per row id: the path and line

criteria.text: Each test that carries an acceptance criterion id asserts what that criterion states
criteria.check_method: Read each test that names a criterion id, then the criterion in its spec

scale.met: each such test fails if the criterion's result is absent
scale.partial: each test exercises the behaviour but one asserts a weaker result than the criterion
scale.unmet: a test carries a criterion id yet asserts nothing about it, or is skipped
scale.evidence: per criterion id: the test name and the asserting line

criteria.text: No file is changed that no task row names
criteria.check_method: Compare the changed paths with the files the rows name

scale.met: each changed path is named by a row
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a changed path has no row
scale.evidence: the changed paths with their row ids

criteria.text: The code prompt tells the session to run only the test files a phase's rows name after that phase, and each verification command of the plan once, after the last phase, with the plan marked completed and the code report written, and to change no file after that run (in the quick lane, the note's `Verify` commands once, after the last criterion and the report, with no file changed after that run)
criteria.check_method: Read the code prompt file of the package for the instructions, phrase by phrase

criteria.text: The code gate runs a verification command only when no result of that command is recorded for the same tree, so a retry or a later visit of the code step on an unchanged tree runs nothing again (CHK-B13)
criteria.check_method: Read the gate's own command runs: each verification command asked for with reuse, none started twice on one tree, and the count taken from a recorded result

criteria.text: A verification command that fails at the gate and fails with the same non-zero exit code at the run's base commit makes the code check return an environmental result, so the gate escalates with no retry and no judge (CHK-B18, CHK-B14)
criteria.check_method: Read the gate's own run of each failing command and its run at the base commit: the same non-zero exit code at both marks the check result environmental

criteria.text: A verification command that fails at the gate and fails with a different non-zero exit code at the run's base commit makes the check environmental when no path the run changed (written from the repository root or from the folder the command ran in) appears in the last lines the command printed at the gate, and fails the check, so the code step retries, when one does
criteria.check_method: Read the gate's run and the base run of each failing command, and look for each changed path, from the root and from the command's folder, in the last lines the command printed at the gate

criteria.text: A verification command that exits 0 at the run's base commit and fails at the gate fails the check, so the code step retries
criteria.check_method: Read the base run of each command that failed at the gate: exit 0 there is a failing finding the step can fix, never an environmental result

criteria.text: A verification command that fails at the gate and was not compared with the run's base commit (the run has no base commit, the command could not start there, or the command did not finish at the gate or at the base) fails the check, so the code step retries with evidence saying the command was not compared
criteria.check_method: Read the gate's run and the base run of each failing command: a missing base commit, a base run that did not start or finish, or a gate run that did not finish is a failing finding that says it was not compared

criteria.text: When a verification command is judged environmental and another finding of the code check also fails, the check fails so that the code step retries with only the findings it can fix listed, while its evidence still names the environmental command
criteria.check_method: Read the code check's findings and evidence: an environmental command is not a failing finding when another finding fails, and its line still leads the evidence

criteria.text: The code check's evidence names each verification command that failed at the gate with its exit code at the gate and at the run's base commit, with the reason it was judged environmental, caused by the change or not compared
criteria.check_method: Read the evidence and the findings of the code check: each failing command has one line with the command, both exit codes and the reason

criteria.text: The engine's check preview is declared on the code step, and the code prompt tells the session to make its one run of each verification command of the plan through that preview
criteria.check_method: Read the code prompt file of the package for the instruction, phrase by phrase; the step's declaration is read by the package's tests

criteria.text: A verification command that exits 0 at the gate is never run at the run's base commit, and one that fails is run there at most once per visit of the code step, however many attempts the visit takes (CHK-B20)
criteria.check_method: Read the gate's own command runs: no base run of a command that exited 0, and a base run asked for with reuse so that a retry of the visit takes it from the recorded result

criteria.text: A preview of the code gate's check, run after the last phase with the plan marked completed, runs each verification command of the plan (in the quick lane, the note's `Verify` commands) and lists each one that fails with its exit code, and reports no failure for the code report the session has not handed over yet or for the commit that follows the session
criteria.check_method: The gate cannot see the session's own run: it records n_a, and the package's tests prove the preview branch of the check

criteria.text: The code gate does not run a verification command again when the session ran it through the check preview on the same tree content, though the session's files were committed after that run (CHK-B13)
criteria.check_method: The gate cannot see the session's own run: it records n_a, and the package's tests prove the reuse across the commit

criteria.text: The code gate runs a verification command again when any file of the tree changed after the session's run of it (CHK-B13)
criteria.check_method: The gate cannot see the session's own run: it records n_a, and the package's tests prove the new run after a change

criteria.text: The code gate's evidence names each verification command of the plan that the gate ran or reused, with the word `reused` or `run`
criteria.check_method: Read the gate's own command runs: one evidence line per verification command, `reused` for a stored result and `run` for a started command

assumptions: Per-phase coding waits for the engine's sequential map; until then a complex plan is coded in one session.
No step or judge uses the large model tier.
Whether the code agrees with the specs by meaning is judged once, at the code gate (ts-code-aligned, ts-code-related), not again at the outcome gate.
The release step and a work-tracker start are left out of the first version.

Verification commands come from the repository's `tempergraph.commands.json` through the engine's `@repository` entry, with read-only git always allowed; prepare writes the Python commands there for a Python repository that has none.

The outcome gate reports whether the run's branch is pushed and never grades it: the last stage pushes after the gate, and a branch an earlier run pushed is already pushed at the gate, so no gate fails a run for the push.

Specs written by the setup step describe behaviour that exists already, so the outcome gate does not ask for a test that names each of their acceptance criteria; a task that later touches such a behaviour adds the id to its test.
Repository setup is a conditional first step of this workflow because release 1 of the engine has no sub-workflows; it moves into one when the engine has them.
The quick lane's limits (3 acceptance criteria, 2 code files, 200 changed lines) are first values with no run behind them; the share of quick runs sent back to triage is the measure to tune them by.
A test carries its criterion as text (the spec's id, or `AC <n>`); the check finds the text and a skip mark near it, and does not prove that the named test is the one the command ran.

The code judge's reading budget (one file per 50 changed source lines, a floor of 10 files and a ceiling of 50) is made of first values with no run behind them; the share of code gates whose judge grades an alignment criterion UNVERIFIABLE for files beyond the budget is the measure to tune them by.

The spec budget is fixed at 400 lines and 30,720 bytes for every repository, with no setting; it is measured once, at discovery (ts-dis-budget), while ts-spec-cap at the outcome gate counts lines only.

The code gate cannot see the session's own run of the verification commands through the check preview, so it records n_a for ts-code-previewed, ts-code-session and ts-code-rerun; the package's tests prove them. ts-code-preview is read from the prompt and ts-code-ran from the gate's own command runs.

No unit criterion serves ts-spec-fresh (OUT-B16), so a failed guard escalates the run at the outcome gate and is not sent back to discovery; a person starts the task again from the head of the base branch.

The triage check given no conversation value reads no sort: the engine's fixture rung gives a check no settings, so ts-tri-owner is not applicable to each triage fixture, and the cases of `never`, `blocking` and `always` are proved by the package's tests.

Two subjects start reading sessions and three run at a time; both are first values with no measured run behind them, and the judges of one gate stay one, each reading gate having a judge of its own (spec parallel-reading, its open questions).

quick lane, proof table, criterion-to-test link and pull request summary, chosen by the owner
plan status and row completion marks checked first at the code gate, requirement and docs links per row, the scope-cut warning, chosen by the owner
faster runs: the covered mark in triage, a reading list in the hand-off, narrow discovery and plan reading, one full code run per visit and its reuse at the gate (task speedup-runs)

criteria about how the run works (narrow reading, the reading list, commands run once, a reused gate result) are checked model-free from the package's prompts and the gate's own command runs instead of asked of a judge, which sees neither (backlog B30); ts-code-once narrowed to what the prompt says; the short discovery visit `discovery_short` with criteria ts-dsh-* (decision record 0003, backlog B21)

ts-traced asks for tests of the criteria a run added or changed, and of old criteria whose behaviour it changed, never of every criterion of an edited spec (backlog B22); ts-spec-links reads the edited specs only, as its text says

issue 57: the discovery check measures every spec against the spec budget of 400 lines and 30,720 bytes and sends an over-budget spec back for a split by capability (ts-dis-budget, ts-dis-over); the structure check reads an id a split moved as defined in the spec it moved to, and a split-off spec may name ids of the spec it was split from (ts-spec-moved, ts-spec-parent)

the code gate compares a verification command that fails with the run's base commit: a failure that was there before the change, or that no changed file touches, escalates as environmental instead of spending a retry (issue 54)

the code gate's evidence states the changed source lines, a reading budget and the changed source files, and the code judge reads them before it grades alignment; every judge brief and the outcome judge's stance ask for the quoted line behind a MET and grade PARTIAL when the only evidence is search lines (issues 55 and 56, spec judge-reading)
